text: Argonaut video packet Being a videographer in the Argonaut is not about making money. If you want to make money go somewhere else, you will earn more. While you will get paid for your work, it is a fraction of what you could be making doing freelance videos or doing videography for almost any other organization. It generally amounts to less than minimum wage. Being a videographer for the Argonaut is about experience — both learning the technical aspects of film production and the social interaction with interview subjects. Another valuable part of being an Argonaut videographer is the student media community — this is perhaps the most rewarding part about being a part of the Argonaut, but it's completely what you make it. If you want to get a lot out of working with student media, you will. If you're not really into it, it might be a waste of time for you. If you are motivated and want to grow and develop in your film production skills while learning how to operate in a newsroom environment with a team, then you should join the Argonaut as a videographer. Requirements: Experience shooting and editing videos and have either a DSLR or similar camera, or a phone with high quality video capabilities. And at least somewhat of an idea about how to capture good audio. Curiosity about the world around you. Self-driven and motivated to create exceptional video content. Videographers should produce at least one video every other week, but there is room for flexibility — whether that is more or less content. Videographers are paid $15-$40 depending on the length, extensiveness, detail and quality of the video. Generally, most shorter simple videos are $15. Videos that required more time and work to produce, generally with several interviews and more editing are $20-25, and well produced long-form videos in the style similar to short documentaries are $30-40. The majority of videos are worth $15-25. Videos made by videographers will be uploaded to the cloud (Google Drive, OneDrive, Dropbox, etc.) and sent to the video editor for approval, then they will be uploaded to our various social and web platforms. It is recommended that videographers find the style and content of videos they like best and stick to them, such as sports or event coverage. But if a videographer wants to branch out and try something new, that is perfectly fine. Videographers are encouraged to collaborate with other people in the Argonaut, such as writers, to get coverage of stories — the video department of the Argonaut isn’t a separate from the Argonaut, it’s part of the whole organization. The video editor will do his best to help you learn, grow and excel at film production if you put effort into it and take things seriously. Let’s make some amazing videos.
